text:
carmen: Morning all — quick async standup for the release lane. What I did: finished the merge conflict resolution for features/telemetry -> release/v3.1. Did the canary deploy to staging. Blockers: one backport (windows-ppc patch) is failing unit tests, and the infra job for perf-tests is flaky. Today: re-run the backport CI, look into perf job, and cut the release branch if green.

ben: thanks carmen. I kicked the backport job again (CI tag: backport-windows-ppc). It failed with the same test timed out in test_buffer_flush. I can reproduce locally on linux with qemu. Suspect a timing flake.

alice: noted. I'll take the perf job flakiness — saw repeated socket timeouts on the runner. Repro steps: run perf-suite with --concurrency 4, the runner drops after ~120s. For now I added a retry wrapper.

ben: pinging @dmitri for the windows patch — do you have context on that driver change? It touched cache invalidation and I wonder if the test needs adjustment.

dmitri: yeah that change was to avoid double-free on older toolchains. The unit test added a slight delay that exposes a race on certain qemu kernels. I'll try a minimal repro and either tighten locks or make test less timing-dependent. Expect a fix in the next hour.

carmen: great. If we get the backport green and perf job stable we can cut the release branch this afternoon. Also two small merge requests require approvals: MR #4121 (api surface) from @ben and MR #4128 (docs) from @alice — please try to review before EOD.

ben: I opened a quick patch for the buffer test to remove the hard sleep, replaced with event wait. snippet:```c
// wait for flush
wait_for_condition(&buf->flushed, 5000);
```

alice: reviewing MR #4121 now. FYI console shows an unrelated deprecation warning from the SDK in staging, filing a separate ticket (ENG-5234).

release-bot: deploy.staging: canary deployment succeeded for release/v3.1 at 10:23 UTC :rocket: (sha: a1b2c3d)

carmen: awesome — thanks @release-bot and everyone. Quick Q: any objections to backporting the perf-optimizations branch into v3.1? It's small but reduces tail latency.

dmitri: +1 from me if tests pass.

ben: +1, prefer to include it. saves ops cost.

alice: +1 but let's hold if it introduces new failures.

carmen: consensus then. I'll cut branch once backport tests and perf job green. Leave any extra PR pings here. :white_check_mark:
